title: grep -c . || echo 0 produces double-zero output in GITHUB_OUTPUT and Python heredocs

root_cause.mechanism: grep -c outputs '0' to stdout AND exits 1 when no matches. The || echo 0 then appends a second '0' to stdout. COUNT becomes '0\n0' (newline-separated double-zero).
downstream_effects: GITHUB_OUTPUT key=0\n0 → Actions rejects bare '0' line with 'Invalid format'
Python heredoc receives variable expansion '0\n0' → '"key": 0\n0,' is two adjacent expressions → SyntaxError: invalid syntax (perhaps you forgot a comma?)
Step exits 1, job fails, monitor cannot report divergence status

fix.shell: Replace '|| echo 0' with '|| true' — grep -c already outputs 0 on no-match; || true suppresses exit 1 without adding output
fix.python_defense: Use int("$VAR".strip() or "0") casts in Python heredocs to guard against any future multi-line expansion

prevention: Code review: flag any 'grep -c PATTERN || echo N' where N equals grep-c no-match output (always 0). Use '|| true' exclusively.
